t: This is the Theatre Royal Haymarket, a West End playhouse that dates back to 1720, which makes it the third-oldest London theatre still in use. The original building stood a little further north in this street. Samuel Foote acquired the lease in 1747, and in 1766 he gained a royal patent to play legitimate drama in the summer months. The theatre has been on this spot since 1821, when John Nash redesigned it. It's Grade I listed, seats 888 people, and the freehold belongs to the Crown Estate.
